pr_title: Disable update polling for Wemo when devices can push updates
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Disable local polling for wemo when a device is confirmed to support local push updates.

Frequent polling can result in wemo devices bouncing in and out of the unavailable status, and sometimes getting stuck unavailable for a period of time. This PR turns off local polling when three conditions are met:

1. The device has been polled at least once.
2. The device poll was successful.
3. The subscription for device push events is active and at least one push event has been received from the device. (Normally, per the UPnP spec, the devices send a push event as soon as the subscription is created).

If the subscription cannot be renewed for any reason, polling will resume until all three conditions are met again.

issue_context.title: Wemo Light Switches show unavailable every few minutes
issue_context.body:
**The problem**

I have six Belkin Wemo devices, three outlet plugs and three regular light switches (not dimmable). The three outlet plugs and one light switch occasionally show unavailable in the logs, maybe once a day at most. The other two light switches toggle between available and unavailable every minute or two. One did not used to do this (ran fine for a week or more, the other one has been doing this for a while). I have an automation that sends me a push notification if one of these two lights gets left on for one hour. After the first time the automation ran and sent the push notification, the other light switch started behaving this way.

I'm running the latest version of Home Assistant Core (2021.1.5) on a Raspberry Pi
I upgraded the Belkin products to the latest firmware versions
I tried rebooting Home Assistant Core and the Light Switches
I know the light switches are connected to WiFi and available as I've been able to turn them on/off with the Wemo App and Apple Home App while Home Assistant showed them as unavailable.

**What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?**

2021.1.5

**What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?**

_No response_

**What type of installation are you running?**

Home Assistant OS

**Integration causing the issue**

Belkin Wemo

**Link to integration documentation on our website**

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/wemo/

> I didn't think Home Assistant needed to poll these devices. I thought they updated Home Assistant via local push.

It does both for most devices. Local push isn't currently working for these situations:
- Insight energy monitoring
- Dimmers
- Devices not on the local network

> Is there a reliable way to get them unstuck?

Mine unstick themselves after a few minutes. I suspect the issue here is that pywemo is too aggressive when it comes to handling connection failures. Normally the poll is one small network request. However when the poll fails, there can be an additional 7+ larger network requests as pywemo attempts to re-discover and re-establish a connection. My theory is that all this extra network activity makes an already slightly bad connection worse.

I've added some extra debugging on my end to try to find the common cases where the poll fails. Once identified my plan is to try to retry the poll rather than doing the more aggressive re-discovery. I want to build up some baseline data first, to capture the size of the issue, before I make these changes. That way I can verify my changes are making things better and not worse :)  It'll take a few days to collect that baseline data. Then I can start working on some fixes.
Sounds good, thank you!

I have a few days of data now. In each of these graph the line colors represent an individual WeMo device on my network and the x-axis is time over a three day period (Feb 6, 7, 8 UTC).

This first graph is a count of the number of times each device switched to the unavailable state in Home Assistant over a 10 minute period.
![Screenshot 2021-02-08 1 30 01 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/289218/107284160-33720c80-6a12-11eb-8203-e5409ea3d24c.png)

The second graph measures 99 percentile seconds it took for each WeMo device to respond when it was polled within a 10 minute period. Home Assistant waits up to 5 seconds for the poll to complete before reporting the state as unavailable. The pywemo library that Home Assistant uses times-out after 10 seconds. This measurement comes from within the pywemo library.
![Screenshot 2021-02-08 1 40 09 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/289218/107284836-30c3e700-6a13-11eb-80ed-7e59ca4f0a0b.png)

The third graph shows the number of times the pywemo library timed-out waiting for the WeMo device to respond over a 10 minute period.
![Screenshot 2021-02-08 1 38 33 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/289218/107284641-f5c1b380-6a12-11eb-904f-b147b1fe627b.png)

I also took a look at the uptime of the devices, to see if reboots could be causing issues. It looks like only one of my WeMo devices rebooted over the last three days, so I don't believe the slowness is the result of the devices crashing.
![Screenshot 2021-02-08 1 43 55 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/289218/107285351-df682780-6a13-11eb-9edd-33c5230943f9.png)

I also tracked the TCP port number used by pywemo to communicate with the device. A change in port number would cause a delay in communications as pywemo needs to discover the device on its new port.
![Screenshot 2021-02-08 1 50 41 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/289218/107285965-cb70f580-6a14-11eb-941e-a8f4b4489a9a.png)

The final graph is measuring the number of seconds it took for the pywemo library to reconnect to a device after a request failed. This graph is sparse on data points because the measurement is only taken when a reconnect happens, and it appears these events are rare. This graph and the one above look correlated to me, meaning that maybe reconnects might only be happening when the port changes.
![Screenshot 2021-02-08 1 56 07 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/289218/107286559-99ac5e80-6a15-11eb-8805-bee370dc17c9.png)


My initial theory for why devices entered and got stuck in the unavailable state was that the reconnections/rediscovery was happening frequently and taking a long time. That doesn't appear to be the case. Rather, it looks like the WeMo devices are either 1) slow to respond in some situations or 2) have intermittent WiFi connectivity issues. Given this result, I don't think there is anything that can be done in terms of improving the polling logic that will have any impact on this issue.

Instead, I've started working on a way to provide Home Assistant information about when Local Push is known to be working (https://github.com/pavoni/pywemo/pull/236). For devices where Local Push works there are some things we can do to solve this issue:

1. We can disable Local Pull entirely.
2. We can stop putting devices into the unavailable state when Local Pull fails.
3. We can possibly decrease the frequency of the Local Pull updates.

Now that we have some data, and pywemo is able to expose whether or not Local Push is working, I'll start working on a PR for Home Assistant that does the things above and see which are reliable and solve the issue. The first option is the simplest in terms of effort but it is also the riskiest in terms of potentially breaking HA for for users with odd/complicated setups. I'll start there and see how the testing goes.

FYI @pavoni & @Spectre5 from the pywemo project in case you have suggestions also.
These seems to be an issue with devices having poor wifi connectivity, right?  Have you tried bumping up the pywemo timeout to something higher, maybe 20 seconds, to see if that fixes it?

@Spectre5 Good idea. I've changed the pywemo timeout to 25 seconds and am giving that a try now. I have also changed the async timeout to 20 seconds:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/c69c493cf963c913a507c7bd0c02804cdb6e8e1e/homeassistant/components/wemo/entity.py#L61

I'll give these changes a day to run and report back tomorrow with an update.

I noticed #13106 which set a more aggressive SCAN_INTERVAL value for all WeMo switch devices.
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/c69c493cf963c913a507c7bd0c02804cdb6e8e1e/homeassistant/components/wemo/switch.py#L16
The default value for the switch and light domains is 30 seconds. Increasing the frequency that polling takes place, like the PR did, would also increase the frequency that the devices go into the unavailable state.
@jbowen014 which model of outlet plugs do you have? It looks like my planned solution doesn't work for WSP080 & WSP090. It does work for for the WLS040 light switches though.

The outlet plug model number I have is WSP080. I have three and they've been working pretty well overall. I looked at the logs and they might show unavailable once a day or once every few days at most (even the one in the same room as the router six feet away), but never for more than 30 seconds or so.

I did notice something else interesting in the logs. The two light switches that were having issues have been doing pretty well the past few days. They've only shown unavailable a few times a day instead of every few minutes. I briefly turned on additional logging for my router a few days ago to see if anything useful would show up. Doing that must have forced some devices to disconnect and reconnect, which probably helped improve things.

@esev does HA try to poll all devices simultaneously?  Maybe that causes some issues if you have a lot of Wemo devices and HA then tries to contact every devices at roughly the same time, and so frequently.  Perhaps it leads to dropped packets or other interference.

I do still see timeouts and unavailable devices even with the values increased to 25/20 seconds.  HA complains about updates that take longer than 10 seconds, and I see many log entries like this now.

```

```

I also realized I made a mistake in how I was recording the two graphs that measure duration (graphs 2 & 6). The default for the library I'm using (Prometheus) is to max out at 10 seconds. I've adjusted that setting up to 200 seconds and am running again.

> @esev does HA try to poll all devices simultaneously? Maybe that causes some issues if you have a lot of Wemo devices and HA then tries to contact every devices at roughly the same time, and so frequently. Perhaps it leads to dropped packets or other interference.

It does appear to poll all of them at once. So maybe the more devices on the network, the worse things get.
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/9a570d7c3215d1196a8a80f4148d4c19bbdde8ec/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py#L612-L618

I've also seen in tcpdump that pywemo sends a lot of network requests when a single service request fails. It ends up polling for the /setup.xml a few times and then fetching all of the service files again. It looked to me like the device was struggling to respond to all those requests, which lead to further timeouts and even more requests. Sometimes it takes a few minutes to get out of that state.

I stopped chasing that temporarily when I saw the duration graphs. I thought those graphs were showing that reconnects were not an issue. But due to my mistake, those graphs were limited to recording a max of 10 seconds. Hopefully I'll have some better data tomorrow.
Sounds good

@esev as you know, pywemo actually does a multi-cast as part of device re-discovery if the backup `_reconnect_with_device_by_discovery` is used.  Maybe that is a good reason to use unicast instead.  Also, even when it is re-discovered through probing in `_reconnect_with_device_by_probing`, it still creates a whole new device object via `device = self.__class__(url, None)`, which will fetch all of the servive files again as you've seen.  Surely we can handle this better within pywemo.

+1 - it does this after the first [service request](https://github.com/pavoni/pywemo/blob/1253cdd32a4c0d63aa628c52cc0420308a1ce322/pywemo/ouimeaux_device/api/service.py#L53) failure too. I've been wondering if it should retry the service call a few times before starting on rediscovery. That's why I was keeping track of the ports that the devices were using. If the ports aren't changing often, and the IPs aren't changing at all, then simply retrying the call should work - no need for rediscovery. At least no need to do it as often as it happens now.
Yup, makes sense

New graphs.

I still see plenty of times where the device shows as unavailable in HA. Even with the the timeouts set to 25/20 seconds.
![Screenshot 2021-02-11 1 45 13 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/289218/107702753-8f859c80-6c6f-11eb-994b-959c89375de2.png)

And now it's clearer that reconnect_to_device takes a while.
![Screenshot 2021-02-11 1 47 59 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/289218/107702951-d5426500-6c6f-11eb-8c39-308db9d517af.png)

This matches with my experience that it can take a few minutes for devices to appear as available again. I'll try to re-arrange things a bit in pywemo.

1. Retry the call itself a few times before attempting rediscovery
2. Don't replace the entire device when it is rediscovered

I'll keep the Prometheus monitoring in place too, so we can see if these changes will have any impact.

I've been having some success in reducing the overall time that a device hangs in the unavailable state. I'm hoping to have a [PR](https://github.com/pavoni/pywemo/compare/master...esev:retries) ready for pywemo tomorrow.

Just to set expectations though, I'm not able to avoid having the devices enter the unavailable state. I can't fix wifi signal strength issues with software. :)  So the devices will still enter the unavailable state. And some devices will flip-flop into the unavailable state more often, when previously they would have just remained in the unavailable state. But the total time spent in the unavailable state will be less. HA is able to reestablish the connection faster.

With my PR, devices should only get into the unavailable state when there are actual wifi connectivity issues. review_comments: Does this need to be reset when the device is unplugged and plugged back in?

That's a nice catch and a good question. 

What should happen is that the device will respond to updates from Home Assistant as soon as it is back on the network, but state updates from when the device is controlled outside of Home Assistant won't be seen right away - for up to 5 minutes - and the current device state won't be picked up till that point either. There is a refresh of the event subscription that happens every 5 minutes. And when that happens, the UPnP spec states that the device will send it's current state as soon as the new subscription is started. So that _should_ pick up any state changes that happened due to the device being unplugged without needing to poll.

In testing this though, I know that there are [two WeMo devices that don't follow the UPnP spec](https://github.com/pavoni/pywemo/pull/236#issuecomment-776115015) and won't send that initial event to update the current state. And so the state of the device will be inconsistent from Home Assistant if the device was On when it was unplugged (WeMo devices default to Off when they are plugged in).

Let's take a pause on this PR. There is a very simple change I can make to pywemo that will solve this edge case. It's easy to detect the case when a new subscription is started vs a renewal. When the device is plugged back in that'll behave as-if a new subscription is started. I'll just reset the boolean that tracks that the subscription has been confirmed at that point. That'll fix this corner case. For devices that follow the UPnP spec, that initial event will update the state in Home Assistant and reconfirm the subscription. And for devices that don't follow the spec, they'll start polling again.

There will still be a period where the device state will be inconsistent, for up to 5 minutes after it is plugged back in. I'm assuming that is okay since unplugging the device and plugging it back in should be a rare event. But please correct me if my assumption is wrong here.
It seems reasonable to have a recovery period after plugging back in the device 👍

This should work now (#46825) with the 5 minute recovery period.

I manually verified everything in the description of https://github.com/pavoni/pywemo/pull/247

Note that `should_poll` only has an effect for `Entity` built in polling mechanism when adding the entity. Ie the registration of the update on interval only happens during entity addition, not on every state update.
